direct.name: ubuntu-minimal
direct.reason: Ubuntu's own definition of a working base system; the floor everything else stands on

direct.name: systemd
direct.reason: init, the unit model every TemplarOS service is written against

direct.name: systemd-boot
direct.reason: the dev/VM image's bootloader (ADR-0006); bare metal uses shim+GRUB per ADR-0004

direct.name: systemd-resolved
direct.reason: one resolver, so NetworkManager and containers do not each invent DNS

direct.name: systemd-timesyncd
direct.reason: clock correctness: apt signature validity and build-set ids both depend on it

direct.name: udev
direct.reason: device enumeration for templar-hwdetect and the compositor's DRM backend

direct.name: kmod
direct.reason: module loading for the kernel/LRM set templaros-kernel version-locks

direct.name: btrfs-progs
direct.reason: the root filesystem is btrfs so deployments can be snapshots (ADR-0004)

direct.name: dosfstools
direct.reason: the ESP is FAT; provisioning formats and checks it

direct.name: e2fsprogs
direct.reason: ext4 tooling for foreign partitions the provisioner may have to read

direct.name: apt
direct.reason: package installation is how a build set is applied and rolled back

direct.name: apt-utils
direct.reason: apt-ftparchive builds the local build-set archive (D2)

direct.name: ca-certificates
direct.reason: HTTPS to the archive and to snapshot.ubuntu.com

direct.name: gnupg
direct.reason: verifying archive signatures, including the TemplarOS archive key

direct.name: iproute2
direct.reason: the minimum network diagnosis a recovery shell needs

direct.name: iputils-ping
direct.reason: the minimum network diagnosis a recovery shell needs

direct.name: sudo
direct.reason: administration without a root login on a single-user developer machine

direct.name: less
direct.reason: reading a journal in a recovery shell without a desktop

direct.name: vim-tiny
direct.reason: editing a unit or a cmdline in a recovery shell without a desktop

direct.name: linux-generic
direct.reason: Ubuntu's GA kernel; the image must boot before the TemplarOS archive is present

direct.name: templaros-archive-keyring
direct.reason: the TemplarOS archive key, sources and pins; without it no TemplarOS package installs

direct.name: templaros-kernel
direct.reason: version-locks kernel, LRM modules and firmware into one tested set (ADR-0007)

direct.name: linux-firmware
direct.reason: Wi-Fi, GPU and audio firmware blobs the reference laptop needs to come up

direct.name: network-manager
direct.reason: the network provider the shell's status surface and portals talk to

direct.name: upower
direct.reason: battery and lid state for the shell and templar-sessiond's power policy

direct.name: power-profiles-daemon
direct.reason: the profile switch templar-sessiond drives; the alternative is per-vendor sysfs guesswork

direct.name: fwupd
direct.reason: firmware updates through a path that is not a vendor's Windows installer

direct.name: udisks2
direct.reason: removable media mounting for Files without giving the shell block-device privileges

direct.name: mesa-vulkan-drivers
direct.reason: the compositor renders through Vulkan on the Intel iGPU (the default output path)

direct.name: libgl1-mesa-dri
direct.reason: GL for Xwayland clients and toolkit fallbacks

direct.name: vulkan-tools
direct.reason: vulkaninfo and vkcube are how `templar doctor` and the hardware probes name the actual output device

direct.name: libvulkan1
direct.reason: the Vulkan loader itself; the drivers above are ICDs behind it

direct.name: libva2
direct.reason: the VA-API library the media stack and the probes call

direct.name: libva-drm2
direct.reason: VA-API over a DRM device — the headless and compositor path

direct.name: libva-wayland2
direct.reason: VA-API for Wayland clients presenting decoded frames

direct.name: libva-x11-2
direct.reason: VA-API for the Xwayland clients that still exist

direct.name: va-driver-all
direct.reason: the VA-API driver set, so decode works on whichever GPU answered

direct.name: intel-media-va-driver
direct.reason: iHD decode for the Intel iGPU; the -non-free build is in multiverse, which distro/base.toml does not enable — the 59 VA-API profiles the hardware lane measured came from the non-free driver on a dev host and are not a TemplarOS number

direct.name: vainfo
direct.reason: the hardware lane's VA-API probe reports what vainfo says, not what the packages imply

direct.name: mesa-utils
direct.reason: glxinfo — the cheap answer to 'which GPU is this GL context on'

direct.name: mesa-utils-bin
direct.reason: eglinfo — the same question for EGL, which is the path the compositor takes

direct.name: templaros-session
direct.reason: the session unit graph: what starts, in what order, under what target

direct.name: templaros-sessiond
direct.reason: the one policy daemon — identity, launch, associations, providers, settings (ADR-0001)

direct.name: templaros-resourced
direct.reason: the resource governor, deliberately a separate crash unit (ADR-0002)

direct.name: templaros-filed
direct.reason: file operations and the shared file index, off the policy daemon's loop

direct.name: templaros-hostd
direct.reason: the single privileged system-bus surface: updates, deployments, drivers (ADR-0003)

direct.name: templaros-boot-health
direct.reason: marks a deployment good or rolls it back; the reason a bad set is survivable

direct.name: templaros-shell
direct.reason: the Home Field and every decorative surface; restartable in half a second

direct.name: templaros-nm-tray
direct.reason: the network control the Home information row launches; TemplarOS ships no system tray, so an applet that only draws an icon is useless here (distro/forks/manifest.toml)

direct.name: templaros-comp
direct.reason: the compositor; nothing else provides a Wayland session (COMPOSITOR.md)

direct.name: templaros-portal
direct.reason: the TemplarOS portal backend: FileChooser, AppChooser, Background, Settings

direct.name: templaros-cli
direct.reason: `templar` — doctor, dev, update; the CLI parity half of every declared action

direct.name: templaros-greeter
direct.reason: the login surface; a session with no greeter is a session nobody can reach

direct.name: greetd
direct.reason: the daemon templaros-greeter is a client of; it owns the login transaction

direct.name: xdg-desktop-portal
direct.reason: the portal frontend every sandboxed app talks to; backends are chosen behind it

direct.name: xdg-desktop-portal-gtk
direct.reason: Print, Email, Notification and DynamicLauncher, which the TemplarOS backend does not implement and which otherwise fail outright for Flatpak apps

direct.name: xwayland
direct.reason: X11 clients still exist and a developer machine meets them weekly

direct.name: polkitd
direct.reason: authorisation for templar-hostd's privileged actions; the alternative is a setuid habit

direct.name: dbus-broker
direct.reason: the bus implementation both session and system buses run on

direct.name: templaros-settings
direct.reason: the settings surface for the policy templaros-sessiond owns

direct.name: templar-files
direct.reason: the file manager the shell's file surfaces and the Files context menu drive

direct.name: kitty
direct.reason: the Terminal provider role's default (templar-session-core/src/providers.rs:157) and the terminal templaros-shell ships /etc/xdg/kitty/kitty.conf for

direct.name: flatpak
direct.reason: the sandboxed application route (ADR-0011); the browser layer is Flatpak refs, not debs

direct.name: fonts-noto
direct.reason: text that renders in more than Latin; the shell rasterises what the system has

direct.name: fonts-noto-color-emoji
direct.reason: emoji in filenames and chat clients render as glyphs rather than boxes

direct.name: xdg-utils
direct.reason: xdg-open is what non-TemplarOS applications call to hand a file back to the session

direct.name: shared-mime-info
direct.reason: the MIME database detection is compared against; detected MIME beats extension

direct.name: desktop-file-utils
direct.reason: the desktop-file database templar-sessiond imports applications from

direct.name: gnome-keyring
direct.reason: the org.freedesktop.secrets provider: nothing else in the tree implements it, so without it a browser cannot store a password and SSH has no keyring

direct.name: pipewire
direct.reason: the audio and screen-capture server the session and portals are written against

direct.name: pipewire-pulse
direct.reason: PulseAudio clients (most of them) reach PipeWire through this shim

direct.name: pipewire-alsa
direct.reason: ALSA clients reach PipeWire through this shim instead of grabbing the device

direct.name: wireplumber
direct.reason: PipeWire's session manager; without it nothing routes and the desktop is silent

direct.name: gstreamer1.0-plugins-base
direct.reason: the GStreamer element set every other plugin package builds on

direct.name: gstreamer1.0-plugins-good
direct.reason: baseline decode for GTK/Qt applications that play sound or video in-process

direct.name: gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad
direct.reason: the codecs the 'good' set leaves out; without it ordinary web video silently fails to decode

direct.name: gstreamer1.0-libav
direct.reason: the ffmpeg-backed decoders — the difference between 'a player exists' and 'the file plays'

direct.name: gstreamer1.0-pipewire
direct.reason: GStreamer capture through PipeWire, which is what the ScreenCast portal hands to a client

direct.name: mpv
direct.reason: a media player that is a deb, not a Snap or a Flatpak the image cannot install; the audio/video row of the daily-driver matrix needs something to open a file with

direct.name: build-essential
direct.reason: cc, ld and the headers every -sys crate in the graph links against

direct.name: git
direct.reason: the build-set id is derived from the git description (templar-build)

direct.name: just
direct.reason: every repository recipe (`just check`, `just deb`, `just image`) is a justfile recipe

direct.name: rustup
direct.reason: the workspace MSRV (1.97) is above Ubuntu's rustc (1.93), and Ubuntu's rustup Conflicts with rustc and cargo, so it is the one Rust package: it installs the pinned toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml. cargo-deb is not in Ubuntu and is installed through it (`cargo install cargo-deb`)

direct.name: mkosi
direct.reason: the dev/VM image builder (ADR-0006); a self-hosting image can rebuild itself

direct.name: pkg-config
direct.reason: how the -sys crates find the libraries build-essential can link

direct.name: orca
direct.reason: the screen reader; note the shell has no AT-SPI bridge yet (docs/architecture/accessibility.md)

direct.name: at-spi2-core
direct.reason: the accessibility bus Orca reads a desktop through

direct.name: speech-dispatcher
direct.reason: the speech backend Orca speaks through

direct.name: fcitx5
direct.reason: one input method, the `input-method` provider role; two would fight over the same protocol

direct.name: fcitx5-config-qt
direct.reason: configuring the input method without editing its config by hand

direct.name: bluez
direct.reason: the Bluetooth stack the shell's status surface and audio routing talk to

flatpak.name: org.mozilla.firefox
flatpak.reason: the daily-driver browser, sandboxed per ADR-0011; Ubuntu's firefox deb is a Snap wrapper, which [policy].conflicts forbids, so the ref is installed from Flathub by first boot (distro/seeds/flatpak-refs.list)

profile: image layers + the default variant of each group
